#uranium #copper #silver #gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — 27 AUGUST 2026 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

Yesterday’s U.S. data gave Fed hawks more ammunition, but the metals complex is refusing to roll over.

Headline and core PCE both rose 0.2% MoM in July, with annual inflation at 3.7% and 3.3%. Durable-goods orders also beat expectations at +1.1%.

Yet the U.S. 10-year yield has eased back to around 4.65% in Asia, DXY is holding near 99.1 and hard assets are rebounding. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech on Friday is now the next major macro catalyst.

☢️ URANIUM — Nearby uranium pricing has moved through $90/lb, its highest level in more than six months.

The U.S. Army has also announced up to $2.2B for five initial military microreactor projects. With private investment included, it expects more than 20 reactors across military installations, with the first targeted for operation in 2028.

This will not transform uranium demand overnight, but nuclear rhetoric continues to become funded deployment.

🟠 COPPER — LME three-month copper finished Wednesday at approximately $14,336/t, just 1.3% below its record.

China’s latest data were mixed: overall industrial-profit growth cooled in July, but profits in non-ferrous smelting and processing surged 91.8% during January–July. Nvidia’s revenue more than doubled, further strengthening the long-term AI and data-centre infrastructure narrative.

Copper continues to absorb a firm dollar, mixed Chinese data and easing near-term tightness without moving far from record territory.

🥈 SILVER — Spot silver is leading the Asian rebound, up 1.7% to around $69.28.

Holding near $70 despite DXY sitting close to a one-week high and Treasury yields around 4.65% shows that buyers remain willing to step in after pullbacks.

🥇 GOLD — Spot gold has rebounded 0.8% to approximately $4,630.

The hotter inflation data and rising probability of further Fed tightening have failed to break the debasement trade. U.S. deficit concerns and the Treasury’s expanded purchases of older long-dated bonds remain powerful support.

The market is being given textbook reasons to sell metals—high yields, a firm dollar and higher rate-hike odds—and it continues to find buyers.

That resilience is today’s signal.

#uranium

Skyharbour Resources ($SYH | $SYHBF) may be testing something much more interesting than an extension of its known Maverick deposit.

What if Moore hosts a series of uranium centres along the same structural corridor?

At Maverick, drilling has already returned grades as high as 20.8% U₃O₈ over 1.5 metres.

To the southwest, drilling at Nomad encountered a broad hydrothermal system with pervasive faulting, clay alteration and silicification – the geological plumbing associated with Athabasca uranium deposits.

Around 3 kilometres northeast of Maverick, Esker has already returned 1.21% U₃O₈ over 0.5 metres.

The 2026 program is now testing all three areas while also targeting the largely unexplored basement beneath Maverick’s known high-grade mineralization.

The real opportunity may be turning Moore from a single high-grade discovery into a much broader uranium system.

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Skyharbour Resources. Please do your own research.

This does not change the fact, the the script has flipped to ACIE having higher growth rates going forward vs. hyperscaler.

CZ said it better than anyone:

"The currency for AI is crypto. AI is not gonna swipe a card, enter an SMS code. That doesn't work for AI."

That was our conversation at Token2049 in Dubai last year. Every month since has made it truer... more agents arriving, all needing to hold value, receive value and move it without a person in the loop.

Think about what those payments actually look like. Instant and tiny, thousands of them a second, between counterparties that are not human. Two day bank settlement doesn't work for that. Card rails don't work for that. 

Theres only one set of rails on earth built for that. Its staggeringly clear.
